en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Gabbhinīvagga 64.
The Second Training Rule for a Sikkhamānā.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were giving the full admission to a *sikkhamānā* who had trained for two years in the six rules but had not been authorized by the Saṅgha.
The bhikkhunīs said to her:
“Come, *sikkhamānā*, know this; give this; bring this; there is need for this; make this allowable.”
They replied, “We are not trainee nuns, noble lady; we are bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... were indignant, disparaged [her], and complained, saying:
“How indeed can nuns give the full admission to a trainee nun who has trained for two years in the six rules, yet has not been authorized by the Saṅgha?

… [The Buddha asked: “Is it true, monks, that nuns are giving the full admission to a trainee nun who has trained for two years in the six rules, even though she has not been authorized by the Saṅgha?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can these bhikkhunīs, monks, give the full admission to a trainee nun who has trained for two years in the six rules but has not been approved by the Saṅgha?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith…” [and so on].
Having rebuked him … and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, bhikkhus, to grant the formal consent for ordination to a training nun who has trained in the six rules for two years.”
And furthermore, monks, it should be granted in this way:
that trainee nun who has trained in the six rules for two years should approach the Saṅgha,
arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhunīs, squat down on her heels, and raise her joined palms.
Having taken hold of her, she should be addressed thus:
“Venerable ladies, I, the trainee nun named so-and-so, who has trained in the six rules under the venerable lady named so-and-so for two years, request the Saṅgha’s consent for my full admission.
She should request it a second time as well.
A third time she should be asked.
A competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha:
“Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
This trainee named so-and-so, having trained in the six rules for two years under the venerable lady named so-and-so, requests the Saṅgha for permission to be admitted.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha grant permission for the admission of this trainee named so-and-so, who has trained in the six rules for two years.
This is the motion.
"Let the Saṅgha, noble ladies, hear me.
This Sikkhamānā named so-and-so, who has trained for two years in the six rules under the noble lady named so-and-so, requests from the Saṅgha permission to go forth.
The Saṅgha grants permission to go forth to this Sikkhamānā named so-and-so, who has trained for two years in the six rules."
Whichever noble lady approves of granting the authorization for ordination to the trainee named so-and-so, who has trained in the training for two years in the six rules, let her remain silent;
whichever does not approve, let her speak.
The Sangha has granted the authorization for ordination to the trainee named so-and-so, who has trained in the training for two years in the six rules.
“The Saṅgha approves; therefore it is silent. Thus do I hold this.
Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support...
[and so forth] ... “And furthermore, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule as follows:”

“Whatever nun, however, should give the full admission to a trainee nun who has trained for two years in the six rules but has not been authorized by the Saṅgha, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Two years" means:
Two years.
"One who has trained in the training" means one who has trained in the six rules.
"Unappointed" means that the formal authorization for ordination has not been granted by means of a legal act consisting of a motion and a second.
"Should ordain" means...
If she should ordain [a woman], or if,
intending "I will give the full admission," she seeks out a group, a preceptor, a bowl, or a robe, or designates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
At the formal motion (ñatti), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
For two formal proclamations (*kammavācā*), there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation, it is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for the preceptor (*upajjhāyā*);
it is an offense of wrong-doing for the assembly and for the teacher (*ācarinī*).
If it is a legitimate legal procedure (*dhammakamma*) and she perceives it as such, yet she ordains [a girl], there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
If it is a legitimate legal procedure but she is uncertain of it, yet she ordains [a girl], there is an offense of expiation.
If it is a legitimate legal procedure but she perceives it as an illegitimate legal procedure (*adhammakamma*), yet she ordains [a girl], there is an offense of expiation.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as a legitimate legal procedure, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one is uncertain of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as an illegitimate legal procedure, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if she gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has been approved by the Sangha and has trained for two years in the six rules;
or if she is insane.
"Regarding the first offender":
thus concludes the fourth training rule.
